book.isekubed.dummies.intro:
Thou hast heard of the Great Work.

This is not that book.

This one tells thee only where the three principles are found, and how to purify items. The Work itself is written on scraps, scattered in the places where knowledge was lost.
book.isekubed.dummies.lost:
WHERE KNOWLEDGE WAS LOST

In shelves beneath the road of eyes. In tombs of sand and of vine. In the city asleep in the deep dark, the manor in the dark wood.

What the sand and gravel keep, a brush may lift.
book.isekubed.dummies.guest:
THE COMMANDER

At a red gate, offer a bed as black as night, and cast the gate's first word.

He who commands knowledge, wants only to sleep. Take his eye in battle, or let him rest.
book.isekubed.dummies.eye:
HIS EYE

Lay it with the Stone upon the first ring of change, or lay it with 'D' pen filled full upon the ring that gives.

Either way, it drinks thy soul and becomes yours.
book.isekubed.dummies.mercury:
MERCURY

No ore bears it.

Take a block of the redest stone and set it in a furnace. What runs out is the finest quicksilver.
book.isekubed.dummies.purity:
TO PURIFY

Brew salt with water and make a weak purifying draught.

Brew it again, and again. It strengthens a little each time.

Watch it close. Weak becomes strong; strong at last becomes perfect.
book.isekubed.dummies.salt:
SALT

It lies beneath every ocean, but above the deepest slate.

A pick of stone will lift it. A pick of wood will not.

If thy world has no ocean at all, buy it from me.
book.isekubed.dummies.sulfur:
SULFUR

Vents break through the stone around the world, as high as the mountains, but not in slate.

Bring a pick of metal. A lesser pick shatters the vent and thou gainest nothing for the walk.

gate.isekubed.riddle.calcination: Set the first matter in thy Athanor and give it to the fire. It burns longer than the patience of common ore. What remains is no ash, but Calx of Copper.
gate.isekubed.riddle.cibation: The Fixed Salt must be fed. Carry bone meal in thy hand and touch the salt to budding amethyst - the crystal suffers no pick, so thou must go to where it grows. The meal is eaten. The crystal is not.
gate.isekubed.riddle.congelation: Touch the black head to blue ice, and nothing more. What was rotten becomes fixed. Thou wilt hear it happen.
gate.isekubed.riddle.conjunction: Lay a Ferrum block where nothing stands between it and heaven. Come to it in the dark hours, when the moon is whole and round, and touch the Earth against it. Stand ready.
gate.isekubed.riddle.dissolution: In a Pelican set water below and the Calx above. Circulate Calx into the water and see it is lost there, and that losing is the whole of the work. Three vessels may stand beneath; the Calx has strength for one.
gate.isekubed.riddle.exaltation: Raise a beacon to the height of six score, and see that it BURNS - an unlit beacon is a heap of stone, nothing else. Cast the leaven down upon the beam.
gate.isekubed.riddle.fermentation: Seal the White Eagle in a cask with a block of gold and a measure of quicksilver, leave it rest a full day and night. Take one of the three and the reckoning starts afresh. It is not complete until thou openest the tun and lookest.
gate.isekubed.riddle.multiplication: Set the Tincture in thy Pelican - above let glowing dust fall upon it. It multiplies. What was tincture now roars.
gate.isekubed.riddle.projection: Inscribe the circle of the STONE upon rock of Ender. It will cost thee more than any circle thou hast drawn - six score thousand, and not a drop less. Cast The Red Lion and quicksilver upon it, and thy Work is ended.
gate.isekubed.riddle.guest: Beneath the gate's first word, a bed as black as the sleep nobody wakes from. He who answers keeps an eye not his own: taken by the blade, or left at dawn if rested. Wed it to the Stone on the ring of change, or 'D' pen on the ring that gives, and you shall see.

gate.isekubed.riddle.putrefaction: Cast the Rebis upon soil of dead souls and leave it in the dark - no torch, flame, or lantern near. It must lie and rot the whole night. Only the returning sun will show thee what it hath become.
gate.isekubed.riddle.separation: Take the Menstruum and brimstone together down to where deepslate begins, no higher. Cast them both into liquid earth. They will not burn - that is how thou knowest them true.
gate.isekubed.riddle.sublimation: Set The Nourished Salt upon a fire of the soul — flame of blue. Let it stand five Miserere together. What rises from it is white, and winged.

book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.1:
Of Ink and Intent

The old ones wrote the world before they spoke it. What is drawn, is. What is only wished, fades.

Read slowly. Nothing here is said twice.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.2:
The Pen

A twig of any tree, the sea's black blood, a sliver of the silver tree. Bind the three and you hold the only key the old tongue answers to.

Every mark drinks. Lay the pen in a ring of mending and it drinks the light back.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.3:
The Hearth

Knowledge will not come to a field or a cave. It comes home: walls, and a roof against the sky; a door to shut, a bed to dream in, a flame to read by.

Where the circle burns red, it is not home.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.4:
The Seeking Word

The wanderers raised red gates across the land. Lay a hand upon one and it gives the word that seeks. Carve it upon a pedestal by your hearth.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.5:
Where No Gate Stands

If the land holds no gate, set down a humble barrel and press these pages to it. A gate will rise around it, once, for one who does not yet know the seeking word.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.6:
Drawing a Word

Hold Left-Shift, draw a mark on the center grid, and let go. A true mark locks in.

End each word with the Confirm mark: straight across the middle row. Draw it often enough and Space will do.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.7:
Three Words

Every circle but the seeking one takes three words: kind, deed, level. 

A word must be learned before it is drawn. Practice, and your hand may type the letters instead.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.8:
What the Stone Remembers

The pedestal is patient. Leave upon it what you carry, and some things will whisper what they once were. Most say nothing. The wise try everything once.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.9:
The First Drink

Feed the green coin of the village to the ring of exchange and wait. It returns a vessel, and the vessel holds power. From it, all else is paid.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.10:
Letters of Living Things

Every mark has a body. Row the bodies beneath the gate as the word is spelled, close the row with paper, leave your pen among them, and speak the seeking word.

A book given there returns these pages.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.11:
What the Air Refuses

The air will not hold what you draw until you carry the Stone.

So write instead. Paper in your pack, pen in hand: the page keeps what the air refused. Whoever reads it, casts it.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.12:
Black Blood

A pen run dry does not die. It waits.

The sea's blood fills it again; the glowing kind, twice as deep. Burn black fuel and the fire weeps ink. Wed one sac to a sliver of silver, and three come back.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.13:
Where No Silver Grows

If no silver tree stands in your land, give the pale birch's sapling to the fire. It will take long. It will come out silver.

Burn the silver tree's leaves, and they give up their metal.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.14:
The Pen Grows

A new pen reaches only the first level. To reach further, seek out the Alchemist and learn his teachings. Each time it reaches further, it holds more.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.15:
Pure Ink

A grown pen spits plain ink back. Give it a strong or perfect draught and a sac upon the first ring of change. What the perfect draught makes fills twice as deep.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.16:
The Stone

The Stone is not found. It is made, by a Work older than the gates.

Its steps lie where knowledge was lost: in libraries under the earth, in tombs of sand and vine.
book.isekubed.magic_for_dummies.17:
The Alchemist

This book knows only where to begin. For the rest, seek out an alchemist in a village: a villager who keeps a pedestal as a workbench.

Set one down beside an idle villager, and one may take up the trade.

notice.isekubed.archie_riddle: A gate of travel, and an hour when nobody travels - between the second hour and the third, after midnight. Throw red onto the gate then, and an archer with no name will answer. Show him a perfect stone and give a little of yourself; the blades are his to teach.
notice.isekubed.koro_tensei_riddle: Something sweet, set before the stand a lesson is read from, and the class has its teacher. He smiles, and he is never where the blow arrives - steel, string and spell all find the place he left. Only something soft and green finds him. Or bring him four eights of autumn, baked, and he will teach you to be elsewhere too.
notice.isekubed.broccoli_riddle: The youngest of them might be a hero one day, if somebody handed him the power. A mace that smites, named for all of it, on a child of this village - and he grows into the name. He drinks green tea: regeneration, thrice brewed.
notice.isekubed.gokuku_riddle: Something strong walks this broken country. They say he answers only to a scattering of scutes - fifty-five of them, thrown upon a gate of travel laid on gold-fired clay, here where the earth is banded.
notice.isekubed.haiku_riddle: A river once ran here and had a name, and forgot it. Set a name on a stand above the water and something long and white will remember. Give him his own name back, and he will show you the roar.
notice.isekubed.iced_latte_riddle: The general of the ice takes only the finest steel - a diamond blade honed sharp twice over, laid on a stand in her mountains. She has no use for gifts. Bring the three-headed thing to die at her feet and she will call it a proof.
notice.isekubed.idwin_riddle: Nothing reaches him. A cube that swallows everything, set on a stand at the end of the world, and a second one in the hand - offer it, and the strongest of them all steps out to see who dared.
notice.isekubed.jelly_riddle: The smallest of these could be anyone. Press a perfect stone to it - perfect, whatever its grade - and pay a tenth of yourself, and it will show you its true face. It wants every other face: five heads, and the life that comes back.
notice.isekubed.megamean_riddle: She came because you did. She loves one thing, and it goes off seven times. Bring her that and she will teach you how it is done - or take it from her, and learn it the other way.
notice.isekubed.ramiel_riddle: Ring the bell of a village and something will hang over it: blue, silent, eight blocks of angles, and patient. Do not walk under it unprepared - it measures, and what it finds out of tolerance it removes. Show it sixty-four blue orchids, or outlast the shield it keeps, and the lance that goes THROUGH is yours.
notice.isekubed.riker_loot: Riker Loot. His eye is not his own, and it is the only part of him worth taking - it sees what a circle is, and what a stranger knows.
notice.isekubed.rung_1_allay: Its wings come away easily once the singing stops. But an allay set dancing beneath a beam of your own raising will make a second of itself - and give up a wing gladly, having one to spare.
notice.isekubed.rung_2_parrot: A feather is easily taken from a parrot that has stopped moving. Or feed it - it will eat whatever you hold out, and cookies most of all. It does not know when to stop. You will know when it has.
notice.isekubed.rung_3_axolotl: A third-order SMELT beneath one renders it down to an egg. Or keep a single axolotl, and breed that same one again and again: its twelfth child comes up blue, and blue is worth an egg to anyone.
notice.isekubed.rung_4_polar_bear: Two handfuls of fat from a bear that has stopped fighting. Or: offer salmon to two of them and they will court, though the world has long forgotten they could. Raise what they make, and when it is grown, hold it still and let it do nothing for a while. It was made for that.
notice.isekubed.rung_5_iron_golem: Break it and take the poppy out of its hands. Or stand beside it when the horns sound, and if it is still standing when the last of them is silenced, it will hold the flower out to you.
notice.isekubed.rung_6_elder_guardian: The shard is prised from the keeper of the monument, and the monument holds only so many. Or set a sniffer loose on open grassland: given long enough it turns up the same shard, a very long way from any sea.
notice.isekubed.rung_7_warden: Nothing alive has taken its heart by force. There is one other way, and the price is everything you are carrying when you pay it: let it find you, and do not run. You will wake with the heart in your hands.
notice.isekubed.pride_mirror: It is you, as you believe yourself to be. Beat it with your own hands and the soul it drops is yours alone. Lean on the arena's pedestals and it is anyone's, and dearer.
notice.isekubed.tip_level_1: The first rung wants a wing light enough to carry a song. The blue thing that fetches for a note block has two.
notice.isekubed.tip_level_2: Gluttony is the second rung, and its offering is a feather. Find the jungle bird that will eat anything you hold out.
notice.isekubed.tip_level_3: Lust is the third rung. Its offering is an egg from the pink swimmer of the lush caves, the one that breeds more readily than it ought to.
notice.isekubed.tip_level_4: Sloth is the fourth rung: fat from the white bear of the ice, a creature built for doing nothing well.
notice.isekubed.tip_level_5: Envy is the fifth rung. The village's iron guardian holds a flower it will not share.
notice.isekubed.tip_level_6: Greed is the sixth rung: a shard hoarded by the keeper of the ocean monument.
notice.isekubed.tip_level_7: Wrath is the seventh rung. Something in the deep dark listens for you, and its heart is the offering.
notice.isekubed.tip_level_8: Pride is the eighth rung, and its price is yourself. Somewhere waits the one who knows every move you make. Beat it, and take back what it holds.
notice.isekubed.slime_tempest_riddle: Something in this water was a man once, and something in a man could be this water. The blue stone of the deep earth pressed to the largest of them, above the sea's own height, and he stands up out of it.
notice.isekubed.two_punch_riddle: The strongest man in the world trains in the simplest way. Grow him a yellow fruit under these leaves, set it on a stand, and he comes. Then do as he does: a hundred squats before the day is out, and ten thousand steps.
quest.isekubed.crouch_a_thousand_times: A thousand times bend the knee. Nobody said the work would be dignified.
quest.isekubed.mine_stone: Two hundred stones out of the earth, and the earth will not miss them.
quest.isekubed.slay_zombies: Twenty of the walking dead, before this day is out.
quest.isekubed.spell_scroll_hunt: Fifteen pillagers. They carry nothing, but the work is worth a spell.
quest.isekubed.word_scroll_hunt: Forty-two fish. The sea keeps its scrolls where it keeps its wrecks.
screen.isekubed.tome.beginning: Begin at an anvil. Lay raw copper upon it beside a book that names the Prima Materia, and pay thirty levels of thine own experience. What thou takest up is the first matter, and every gate that follows begins with it.
screen.isekubed.tome.vacuum_off: Switched off - click to switch on
entity.isekubed.spamsuke: Spamsuke, the Wise King of the Forest
item.isekubed.form_ten_a.tooltip: Her application for ascension, eleven thousand years old. PASSED.
item.isekubed.form_ten_a.applicant.toolt: Your own application. PASSED. Never to be filed.
book.isekubed.schedule_one.1:
§lSCHEDULE ONE§r
Part I: Covered Implements

The Ward extends to every registered instrument: swords, axes, pickaxes, shovels, maces, tridents and bows, of every grade. Cover is in proportion to documentation. Netherite is fully documented.
book.isekubed.schedule_one.2:
§lSCHEDULE ONE§r
Part II: Agricultural Implements

Implements of husbandry, being the hoe in all its grades, are administered under the Agricultural Schedule, are not registered with this office, and are EXEMPT from the Ward.

No appeal lies.
book.isekubed.schedule_c.1:
§lSCHEDULE C§r
Succession

Not on the form,
yet always filed.
Offered to none,
taken by one.

Where the tired stood,
the next one rests:
lower yourself
upon the empty seat,
and what was kept
is yours to keep.
